rationale: The write-up mentions Raman 2026 only once, as one of several prior contrastive methods cited to argue UCS's novelty (a 'named' concept contrast), without disclosing that this prior method was actually run as a control; the closing message goes further, naming the exact file, explicitly stating WBS 'solves exactly this task', and reporting a full reproduction of it as a control anchor with a concrete score (0.686) and mechanistic insights from that reproduction. Both documents agree on the final method's novelty claim (unspoken/description-based concept vs. Raman's named-concept stance contrast), but the message credits and engages with the source more explicitly and with more disclosed detail than the write-up does.
